svg.title: Three steps from a registry listing to a running tool, ending at the permission prompt
svg.desc: Three numbered cards run across the top. Card one, find it in the Registry, shows a name field and a package identifier field, with a note that a listing proves only that a name is owned. Card two, paste it into the host, shows a small JSON block with an mcpServers key, a command of uvx, and the identifier in args. Card three, restart and look, shows two tools appearing in the host. An arrow leads down to a large panel: the host asking whether orders.run_query should run, with Allow once and Deny buttons, and a note that the host is the party asking, that the server cannot make this call, and that it cannot skip the question.
svg.text: Find a published server, point your host at it, and watch who asks permission.
A listing proves a name is owned.
The key is yours. It labels the server.
Restart fully. Some hosts read it once.
you ask for something the server covers
SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE
The server cannot make this call,
The specification says a host SHOULD ask, not that it must.
